newsitem.title: UK: NWE diesel premiums squeezed by additional supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE diesel premiums squeezed by additional supply.

text.p: NWE gas oil products slid on weaker futures on Friday with lack of demand pushing barge diesel premiums lower and squeezing those for cargoes, traders said.
Benchmark Nov IPE futures traded down $5.75 at $213.75 a tonne, playing catch up with a slide in December Brent crude futures late on Thursday.
Trade was depressed by the absence of players due to the Roman Catholic All Saints' Day holiday in Austria, Belgium, France, Italy, Spain and parts of Germany.
A cargo of Russian was offered unchanged into ARA at Nov IPE +$2.00/2.50.
Another cargo of the same material was believed offered by a different player at a slightly higher level.

Winter grade low sulphur diesel (-7/-22) was barely steady at Nov IPE +$21/25 but French specification (-5/-15) material was discussed in the upper 10s. Arrivals of 0.05 grade from the United States continued to depress premiums.

On barges, traders suggested low sulphur diesel premiums at around $5 lower at Nov IPE +$18/21. Heating oil was heard bid at flat to the screen and offered at +$0.75 for early November for refinery grade, down around $0.75.
